title: 2002 HMMT February Team Problem 4
statement:
Let \(n\) be an integer. Prove that

\[\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor+\left\lfloor\frac{n+1}{2}\right\rfloor=n .\]

solutions.text: Suppose \(n=2 m\) is even. Then \(\lfloor n / 2\rfloor=\lfloor m\rfloor=m\) and \(\lfloor(n+1) / 2\rfloor=\lfloor m+1 / 2\rfloor=m\), whose sum is \(m+m=2 m=n\). Otherwise \(n=2 m+1\) is odd. In this case \(\lfloor n / 2\rfloor=\lfloor m+1 / 2\rfloor=m\) and \(\lfloor(n+1) / 2\rfloor=\lfloor m+1\rfloor=m+1\), whose sum is \(m+(m+1)=2 m+1=n\), as desired.
